question: A 17-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her mother because she has not had her menstrual period yet. At birth, she had ambiguous genitalia. The mother reports that during the pregnancy she had noticed abnormal hair growth on her chin. A year ago, the girl broke her distal radius after a minor trauma. She is at the 95th percentile for height and 50th percentile for weight. Physical examination shows nodulocystic acne on the face, chest, and upper back. Breast development is at Tanner stage I. Pelvic examination reveals normal pubic hair with clitoromegaly. A pelvic ultrasound shows ovaries with multiple cysts and a normal uterus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Ambiguous genitalia at birth" -> "Abnormal hair growth on chin during pregnancy" -> "Clitoromegaly on pelvic exam" -> "Multiple cysts on ovaries on ultrasound" -> "Nodulocystic acne on face, chest, and upper back" -> "Breast development at Tanner stage I" -> "95th percentile for height, 50th percentile for weight" -> "Polycystic ovary syndrome" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Distal radius fracture after minor trauma" -> "Increased androgen levels" -> "Clitoromegaly on pelvic exam" -> "Multiple cysts on ovaries on ultrasound" -> "Nodulocystic acne on face, chest, and upper back" -> "Breast development at Tanner stage I" -> "95th percentile for height, 50th percentile for weight" -> "Polycystic ovary syndrome" -> 90%
analysis: The most likely diagnosis for this 17-year-old girl with ambiguous genitalia, clitoromegaly, nodulocystic acne, multiple ovarian cysts, and absent breast development is Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS). PCOS is characterized by hyperandrogenism, menstrual irregularities, and polycystic ovaries on ultrasound. The presence of clitoromegaly, acne, and ovarian cysts along with the other symptoms point towards PCOS as the most likely diagnosis.
